- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.50) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting toward historical mean after volatility), reduce forecast magnitude by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment direction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00–0.50), model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid missing downward trend.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of a 30-day window, reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 5–7 days to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
